name: DoD and Test Linkage Patterns (Xray, Zephyr, TestRail, Smart Checklist)
summary: Definition of Done and test-case linkage are almost never first-class in modern work-tracking tools — both are implemented through a fragmented ecosystem of Marketplace add-ons that bolt structured fields onto Jira's otherwise free-form description. For DoD, the dominant pattern is checklist apps (Smart Checklist by TitanApps, Checklists for Jira by HeroCoders) that add a custom field with templates, mandatory items, workflow validators that block transitions, and a 'Checklist Progress %' field that can be surfaced on the board card face. Atlassian's late-2024 native Action Items feature deliberately stays informal — checkboxes inside the description rich-text editor with no assignment, no templates, no JQL, no automation — so it does NOT replace the checklist app ecosystem for serious DoD work. For test linkage, three tools dominate with different data architectures: Xray stores tests as native Jira work items and exposes a 'Requirement Status' custom field with five values (OK / NOK / NOTRUN / UNKNOWN / UNCOVERED) plus colour that can be added to card layout as a coverage badge; Zephyr Scale stores tests in its own database and adds a Zephyr panel to the issue view with linked test cases, cycles, and executions; TestRail keeps tests in TestRail and adds a 'TestRail: Results' section plus a Jira Coverage Check that audits Sprints / Fix Versions / Epics for untested stories. Across all three test tools and all checklist apps, the card face stays mostly empty by default — surfacing a coverage badge or DoD progress on the card requires explicit Card Layout configuration, which most teams never do. The composite traceability signal (✓ code · ✓ tests · ✓ DoD) does not exist natively in any of these tools — it is a real gap that an EAP prototype could fill.
card_surface: Almost nothing appears on the card face by default — DoD and test status are panel/detail features, not card-surface features. Per tool: Xray surfaces a 'Requirement Status' coloured pill on the card ONLY if an admin explicitly adds it via Board > Configure > Card Layout — the pill renders one of five values with distinct colours (OK green, NOK red, NOTRUN grey/amber, UNKNOWN purple, UNCOVERED grey/white). Smart Checklist and Checklists for Jira each expose a 'Checklist Progress %' or 'Checklist Progress' read-only numeric field that, when added to card layout, renders as a short text label like '7/10' or '70%' — neither app draws a progress bar on the card face by default, though Checklist for Jira (Okapya) renders a thin horizontal bar on Agile cards as an opt-in. Zephyr Scale and TestRail do NOT expose any card-face indicator — both surface their data exclusively in the issue detail view, and a developer scanning a board cannot tell from the card whether tests have been linked, run, or passed. Atlassian Action Items render as inline checkboxes inside the description rich text and have no card-surface representation at all — they are invisible until the issue is opened. Net effect: on a standard Jira board with no marketplace customisation, the card face carries zero DoD signal and zero test signal. Teams that care must explicitly buy the apps AND configure Card Layout — a two-step burden most never complete.
detail_panel: The detail panel is where these tools earn their cost — each adds a distinct section to the issue view. Xray adds a 'Test Coverage' panel on requirement-typed issues (issue types mapped to 'Requirement Issue types' in Xray's admin), showing the Requirement Status badge, a list of linked Tests with their last execution status (PASS / FAIL / TODO / EXECUTING / ABORTED), test environment, and click-through to each Test issue. Because Xray Tests are native Jira issues, they also appear in the standard 'Issue Links' section with link types 'tests' / 'is tested by'. Zephyr Scale adds a collapsible Zephyr section to the issue view — clicking the Zephyr logo reveals subsections for linked Test Cases, Test Cycles, and Test Executions, each with status, executor, and timestamp; the panel exposes 'Add Existing Test Case' and 'Create Test Cycle' actions inline. TestRail adds a 'TestRail: Results' section below the description (collapsed by default, must be expanded via three-dot menu the first time), plus right-rail 'TestRail: Cases' and 'TestRail: Runs' widgets showing linked cases/runs with pass/fail counts pulled live from TestRail. Smart Checklist and Checklists for Jira each add a dedicated 'Checklist' section to the issue view with the full checklist rendered inline — items with status (open / in-progress / done / skipped / N/A), mandatory markers, due dates, assignees, expandable detail fields, and reusable template applicator. Atlassian Action Items are inline in the description/comment rich text — there is no separate section; checkboxes sit wherever the user typed them. [uncertain] Exact placement (above vs below description) varies by Jira Cloud release and is being reshuffled by the new Jira UI rolling out across 2025-2026.
state_coupling: Strong for DoD via checklist apps, weak for test linkage. Smart Checklist and Checklists for Jira both ship 'workflow validators' that can be attached to any transition in a company-managed Jira workflow — the validator blocks the transition unless every checklist item (or every mandatory item) is marked done. Smart Checklist exposes two validator flavours: 'All checklist items completed' and 'All mandatory checklist items completed' — the second allows non-mandatory items to remain open while still gating on critical quality items. This is the canonical DoD gate: a developer cannot move a story to Done unless the DoD checklist is complete. Both apps also integrate with Automation for Jira so templates can be auto-applied on issue creation, on transition into a status, or on changes to a label or component. For test linkage, state coupling is weak: Xray, Zephyr, and TestRail do NOT block work item transitions on test status by default — a story can be moved to Done with all linked tests in FAIL or NOTRUN. Teams add this gate manually via Automation for Jira rules that check the Xray Requirement Status custom field, or via ScriptRunner conditions on the transition. Atlassian Action Items have NO state coupling at all — they are pure presentation, not searchable by JQL, not addressable by Automation, and not connected to any workflow validator. This is the single biggest functional gap between native Action Items and the marketplace checklist apps.
draft_vs_ready_state: Not applicable to DoD or test linkage in the PR sense — neither concept has a 'draft' vs 'ready' axis. However an analogous distinction exists: Smart Checklist items support five statuses (open / in-progress / done / skipped / N/A) which can encode 'work in progress on this item' vs 'item complete', and mandatory vs non-mandatory items act as a 'must clear before Done' vs 'guidance only' axis. For test linkage, Xray exposes test execution status (TODO / EXECUTING / PASS / FAIL / ABORTED) and ABORTED + TODO together play the role of 'not ready' — but this is per-test-run, not per-test-case. None of the test tools and none of the checklist apps surface a card-face 'this DoD is in progress vs complete' indicator distinct from the raw progress percentage. Atlassian Action Items have no in-progress state — items are either checked or unchecked, a binary that mirrors the lightweight intent of the feature.
review_state: Not applicable in the PR-reviewer sense, but a related concept exists for checklist apps: Checklists for Jira (HeroCoders) Pro/Enterprise allows individual items to be assigned to a specific user and to require that user's tick to mark complete — effectively turning a DoD item into a per-person sign-off. Smart Checklist Pro supports the same per-item assignee model with @-mentions. Neither surfaces 'awaiting sign-off' as a card-face pill — assignment is visible only when the checklist is expanded in the detail panel. For test linkage, Xray test executions have an 'Executor' field (the user who ran the test) and Zephyr cycles have a similar executor/assignee — these are surfaced in the detail panel test rows but never on the card face. TestRail's Jira widget shows the assigned tester per linked run. Atlassian Action Items have no assignee field — this is one of the major documented gaps versus the marketplace apps and the single most-cited reason teams keep paying for Smart Checklist.
dod_checklist: This is the core question for this research and the picture is consistent across the ecosystem: DoD is implemented via Marketplace checklist apps in 95%+ of serious Jira shops, with Smart Checklist (TitanApps), Checklists for Jira (HeroCoders), and Issue Checklist as the dominant choices and a long tail of others (Easy Checklist, Multiple Checklists for Jira, Checklist by Okapya). All of them implement the same core pattern: a custom field that renders an interactive checklist with status per item, support for reusable templates that can be assigned per issue type / project / scope, mandatory vs optional items, per-item assignees and due dates, automation hooks for template application, and a workflow validator that blocks transitions until items are complete. Completion percentage is exposed as a derived numeric custom field ('Checklist Progress %' or similar) that can be added to card layout — this is the closest thing to a card-face DoD indicator any tool provides. Sub-task based DoD is the budget alternative used by teams without a paid app, but it pollutes the issue navigator and lacks template support. Atlassian's late-2024 native Action Items deliberately did NOT compete in this space — the feature is informal checkboxes in description rich text, no templates, no assignment, no automation, no JQL, no workflow gates, and Atlassian's RFC explicitly framed it as 'lightweight notes' rather than 'structured DoD', signalling that the Marketplace checklist apps remain the only credible path to enforced DoD in Jira. Outside Jira: GitHub Issues uses markdown checklist syntax (`- [ ]` / `- [x]`) which renders as native checkboxes and surfaces task-list completion on the issue card and in linked-issue rollups, and ZenHub's GitHub overlay reads these into a 'Task Progress' bar — this is the closest any tool gets to first-class DoD outside the Jira marketplace model.
test_linkage: Three tools dominate Jira's test management ecosystem, each with a distinct data model. Xray (Xpand IT) stores tests as native Jira work items (Test, Pre-Condition, Test Set, Test Plan, Test Execution) — every test is a Jira issue with its own key, appears in JQL, and links to requirement issues via 'tests' / 'is tested by' link types. Xray exposes a 'Requirement Status' custom field on requirement-typed issues with five values (OK / NOK / NOTRUN / UNKNOWN / UNCOVERED) computed from the union of linked test execution statuses; this field can be added to card layout as the closest thing to a card-face coverage badge, and it appears as a coloured pill in the Xray Test Coverage panel on the issue detail view. Zephyr Scale (SmartBear) stores tests in its own database — they are NOT Jira issues, so they don't appear in JQL but they do appear in the Zephyr panel on the issue with linked Test Cases, Test Cycles, and Test Executions; Zephyr provides built-in dashboard gadgets and a Traceability Matrix that walks Requirements -> Tests -> Test Executions -> Defects. Zephyr does NOT expose a card-face coverage status by default. TestRail (Gurock/Idera) is the most loosely-coupled — tests live entirely in TestRail and the Jira app surfaces a 'TestRail: Results' panel section plus right-rail widgets showing linked Cases and Runs with live pass/fail counts pulled from TestRail; TestRail 10 added 'Live Jira Data Inside TestRail' which inverts the flow. TestRail also provides a 'Jira Coverage Check' that scans a Sprint / Fix Version / Epic for untested stories — a coverage gap audit rather than a per-card badge. Across all three tools, CI pass/fail is treated as a separate signal from functional/acceptance test management: CI lives in Jira's Development panel Builds row, Xray/Zephyr/TestRail live in their own panels, and no native unification exists. The card face stays empty by default; surfacing a test signal requires explicit Card Layout configuration, and only Xray's Requirement Status field gives a meaningful at-a-glance coverage colour.
cicd_status: Not the core scope of DoD or test-management apps but worth noting the boundary. None of Smart Checklist, Checklists for Jira, Xray, Zephyr Scale, or TestRail directly surface CI pipeline status — that signal lives in Jira's native Development panel Builds row, fed by webhooks from Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Bitbucket Pipelines, CircleCI, etc. The conceptual split is deliberate: CI runs unit/integration tests (low-level, fast, automated, gating PR merge), while Xray/Zephyr/TestRail manage functional/acceptance/regression tests (higher-level, often manual or semi-automated, gating release). Xray Cloud's REST and CLI interfaces DO allow CI pipelines to POST test execution results into Xray (e.g. a Jenkins job uploads JUnit XML to Xray, which updates Test Execution issues), which means a green CI build can flip Xray's Requirement Status to OK — but this is a configurable integration pattern, not an out-of-the-box feature. Zephyr Scale offers a similar API ingestion pattern via Zephyr's REST endpoints and the Zephyr CI/CD bridge. TestRail's API CLI uploads results from CI to TestRail runs. In all three cases, the card-face signal stays separate: Development panel builds row for CI status, test-management panel for functional test status, and the developer must mentally combine them. A failing CI run does NOT automatically mark a linked Xray Requirement as NOK unless the pipeline is configured to push results in that shape. [uncertain] Some Xray + Jenkins shops report that they have wired this end-to-end but the exact UX of card-face state composition is implementation-specific.
release_tagging: Cross-cutting concern that DoD and test-management tools relate to via Jira's native Fix Version field. Xray Test Plans and Test Executions can be associated with a Fix Version, allowing 'tests run for version 2.4' to be filtered and reported — Xray's Test Coverage Report can be scoped to a version and shows which requirements in that release have passing/failing/uncovered tests. Zephyr Scale supports a similar Test Cycle versioning model — cycles can be tagged to a version, and the Traceability Matrix can be filtered by release. TestRail uses its own Milestone concept, which can be mapped to a Jira Fix Version via the integration so that a TestRail Milestone aligns with a Jira release; TestRail's Jira Coverage Check explicitly accepts Fix Version as a scope. Smart Checklist and Checklists for Jira do NOT directly relate to release tagging — checklist items live on individual issues, and 'DoD complete for version 2.4' would be computed by aggregating Checklist Progress % across stories with Fix Version = 2.4 (not a built-in view, requires JQL or a dashboard gadget). Atlassian Action Items have no relationship to release tagging at all — they are description-text artefacts. Net pattern: the test tools all integrate with Fix Version as a release-coverage scope, but none of them put the release tag on the story card alongside the test status — both signals live in the detail panel.
aggregation: Substantially better than the PR/branch aggregation gap for parent issues, because test tools were designed around release-scope rollups from inception. Xray's Test Coverage Report aggregates Requirement Status across all child stories of an Epic, all stories in a Fix Version, all stories in a Sprint, or all stories in a Component — output is a coverage matrix with counts per status (OK / NOK / NOTRUN / UNKNOWN / UNCOVERED) and a percentage. Xray dashboards include gadgets ('Overall Requirements Coverage', 'Test Sets per Status', 'Test Plans per Status') that compute these rollups at the dashboard level. Zephyr Scale offers 26+ out-of-the-box reports including the Traceability Matrix which aggregates from Requirement -> Tests -> Executions -> Defects, and gadgets for execution scorecard by cycle. TestRail's Jira Coverage Check is the most aggregation-focused feature in the test ecosystem: it audits an entire Sprint, Fix Version, or Epic and reports which child stories are linked to tests vs unlinked, then exports the gap list. For DoD aggregation, neither Smart Checklist nor Checklists for Jira surfaces a parent-level rollup natively — a Feature card with five child stories does NOT show '3 of 5 stories have DoD complete' on the card face or in the panel. Teams build this via Automation for Jira rules that copy a child's checklist progress to a custom field on the parent, or via Marketplace apps (JXL for Jira, Time in Status for Jira) that compute child-aggregated views. Atlassian Action Items have zero aggregation — items are not even searchable by JQL.
environment_deployment_target: Out of scope for DoD/test-management apps in the direct sense, but two integration patterns matter. First, Xray and Zephyr both expose a 'Test Environment' field on Test Executions — a single test can be executed in 'dev', 'staging', or 'prod' and the execution row records which environment it ran in. The Test Coverage panel in Xray groups executions by environment, so a requirement can be OK in staging and NOK in production simultaneously, which is the closest thing in this ecosystem to a per-environment signal on a work item. Second, none of these tools surface deployment-environment state on the card face — deployment data lives in Jira's native Deployments row in the Development panel, fed by deployment webhooks from CI/CD providers (Bitbucket Pipelines, GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines), and is distinct from test environment metadata. Smart Checklist and Checklists for Jira have no concept of environment — they are pure DoD presentation. The honest assessment: per-environment test status (Xray Test Environment) is the most interesting deployment-related signal in the test ecosystem but it is locked inside the detail panel and never surfaces on the card.
traceability_completeness: This is the central gap that DoD + test linkage research surfaces — and the most valuable insight for an EAP prototype. No tool in this ecosystem natively surfaces a composite '✓ code · ✓ tests · ✓ DoD · ✓ deploy' indicator on the card face or in the detail panel. The component parts exist as separate signals (Development panel for code + CI + deploy, Xray Requirement Status pill for tests, Checklist Progress % for DoD) but they are never synthesized into a single traceability glyph. Xray's Test Coverage Report, Zephyr's Traceability Matrix, and TestRail's Coverage Check each provide a partial rollup — test coverage scoped to a release or epic — but none of them combine test coverage with code state or DoD state. Jira Align (Atlassian's enterprise SAFe tool) exposes a fuller traceability rollup at the feature/epic/portfolio level including connected code, tests, and deployments, but Jira Align is a separate product layered on top of Jira and not visible in standard Jira boards. Targetprocess exposes a similar traceability ring on its cards but only for items it natively tracks (no Xray/Zephyr/TestRail integration). The pattern of a single composite indicator on the card face — say, a four-segment progress arc or four-dot strip where each dot lights up as code lands, tests pass, DoD completes, and a deploy occurs — is genuinely absent across this ecosystem. An EAP prototype that surfaces this single glyph would not be copying any tool; it would be filling a real, observed gap. The Rams test: every Jira shop today has to read four separate fields to know if a story is truly Done — that is precisely the kind of cognitive load a senior designer should reduce.
design_pattern: Four distinct UI patterns operate in this ecosystem, and only one of them appears on the card face. Pattern 1 — Card Layout custom field (Xray Requirement Status, Smart Checklist Progress %, Checklists for Jira Progress): a single inline label or coloured pill added via Board > Configure > Card Layout, monochrome at most 12px, only renders if explicitly configured by an admin. Xray's pill encodes status in colour (OK green, NOK red, NOTRUN amber/grey, UNCOVERED grey), while Smart Checklist's progress field renders as a flat text fraction or percentage with no visual weight. Pattern 2 — Detail panel section (Xray Test Coverage panel, Zephyr panel, TestRail Results section, Smart Checklist field): a collapsible block in the issue detail view, typed-row layout, usually below the description, with inline actions for linking and creating items. Order varies by tool but all four render with the same visual grammar: section header, optional summary line, expandable list of typed rows, click-through to source. Pattern 3 — Inline rich-text checkboxes (Atlassian Action Items): pure description-embedded `[ ]` / `[x]` markdown-style checkboxes with no field, no template, no panel, no progress — the lightest possible pattern. Pattern 4 — Dashboard gadget rollup (Xray Overall Requirements Coverage, Zephyr Traceability Matrix, TestRail Coverage Check): a release-scope or epic-scope coverage report, not on the card or the detail panel but on a separate dashboard or report page. The dominant card-face pattern is icon-absent — most teams ship Jira boards with no test or DoD signal on the card at all because the configuration burden is high and the signal density per card is already crowded. For an EAP prototype the design lesson is that any card-face signal must EARN its place: a single composite traceability glyph (Rams test passes) is a better choice than five separate icons (Jira pattern, fails the Rams test).
